Rust translation of the eight legal Jazzy transitions. UNKNOWN is not installed for invalid operations; invalid transitions return an error, retaining original state.

Translated terminal result retention and expiry. Rust provider owns goal state and pending result waiters; query correlation remains in transport. Core result_timeout default 10s follows rcl; Python facade passes rclpy 900s.

Translated goal/accepted/cancel/execute callback order and default behavior: accept, schedule execute, reject cancel by default; unfinished execution aborts; a callback exception after terminal preserves terminal status with default result. Provider Rust owns state; Python executor owns business callbacks.

Ported the existing get_result-only timeout policy: no application deadline maps to u64::MAX milliseconds on the Zenoh query, one query, AllComplete target, no consolidation. This is a finite protocol bound, not mathematical infinity. Explicit finite wait and local close remain supported; ordinary Service None is unsupported.
Translated the two original UUID/stamp cancellation-selection branches and existing return codes; no owner/recovery token or additional goal state.

Original native-handle facade follows ClientGoalHandle names, accepted/stamp/UUID observations, per-goal feedback filtering and get_result/cancel futures. Callback dispatch is Python executor work; authoritative status remains at provider Rust.

Adapted the fixed DirectNode default of 0.5 seconds (line 23) and active full-window discovery before graph inspection (lines 60-66). All AOS list commands and doctor report start one bounded liveliness snapshot immediately, count it toward the 0.5-second window, wait the remaining time even when entities are already visible, then return only a fresh final snapshot. Zenoh 1.10.1 src/api/session.rs:2881-2955 sends a stateless Current interest per snapshot and lines 3321-3330 finish it on DeclareFinal; its query timeout does not mean a minimum discovery interval. Earlier snapshots are discarded rather than merged, preserving observed removals. Help describes finite discovery, not global readiness or a confirmed Zenoh defect. No daemon, central cache or business-request retry is added.

Follows rclpy wait_for_service/wait_for_server bool, timeout and None behavior, using native availability before a separately invoked single business request. rmw_zenoh availability reads graph service identity; AOS polls existing liveliness snapshots every at most 50 ms, requiring Service/ActionServer kind plus exact name/type/hash, without a new cache or transport interface. ActionServer declares its identity after its five protocol entities; discovery is an observation, not a guarantee that a subsequent request succeeds. Zero/negative timeouts perform one immediate snapshot; finite timeout returns false; native entity/context closure remains Closed/InvalidStateError, consistent with rclpy's final availability check reaching rcl node/context validation. PyO3 releases the GIL and Python holds no duplicate readiness state. No business retry is added.

Root/Action help and every Action command schema publish numeric GoalStatus 0-6 and CancelGoal return_code 0-3 mappings using existing core constants. Terminal values are explicit. Documentation preserves the provider-owned state and distinguishes accepted cancellation from terminal CANCELED; ERROR_NONE alone is not proof that any goal accepted cancellation. Runtime wire values and state transitions are unchanged.

Vendors the exact published zenoh 1.10.1 crate and gates nonempty cached liveliness history ahead of subsequent live callbacks. Original drop notifier remains inside the gate; callbacks run outside session/gate locks. Explicit close releases pending events; replay panic recovers future live delivery. No tombstone or version upgrade. Deterministic helper and real TCP tests cover ordering, reentry, panic/drop, close, and same-session same-token reconnect. Cross-session instantaneous readiness is not a synchronization guarantee.
